answer.summary: No existing open-source tools extend BigBench with memory-aware evaluation under token budgeting and explicit memory state tracking
answer.content: After two review cycles, consistent evidence confirms the absence of any BigBench extensions meeting the specified criteria. All inspected sources either address privacy risks or inference efficiency without evaluating memory under token constraints or providing transparent metrics on memory state usage. The gap remains unbridged, reinforcing the need to pivot toward broader evaluation frameworks beyond BigBench. A bounded revision is requested to explore non-BigBench agent evaluation benchmarks with token budgeting and memory tracking capabilities before finalizing the direction of research.
answer.search: 'memory-aware agent evaluation' 'token budget' 'memory state tracking' 'non-BigBench' 'agent benchmark' in title:github.com huggingface.co
answer.nextTask: Investigate non-BigBench agent evaluation benchmarks with explicit documentation of memory state tracking and usage metrics under token budgeting, focusing on publicly available repositories and peer-reviewed literature. Include a comparative analysis of at least two distinct frameworks for memory-aware agent evaluation under constrained resources.
answer.lesson: When evaluating agent memory systems, require explicit, primary-source evidence from controlled experiments with token budgeting and transparent memory state tracking to avoid conflating operational efficiency with genuine evaluation capability
